source.title: Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities and the Numerical approximation of singular integrals for exponential weights: Methods, Results and Open Problems, Some new, some old.

accepted.question_text: Let I=(c,d) with -infinity <= c < 0 < d <= infinity. Let w:I -> (0,infinity) be an admissible exponential weight in the following sense: Q=log(1/w) is continuously differentiable and Q(0)=0; Q' is nondecreasing on I and Q(x) tends to infinity as x approaches c from the right and d from the left; T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x), for x != 0, is quasi-increasing on (0,d), quasi-decreasing on (c,0), and satisfies T(x) >= lambda > 1; for some epsilon_0 in (0,1), T(y) is comparable to T(y(1 - epsilon_0/T(y))) for y != 0; and for every epsilon > 0 there is delta > 0 such that the local integral of |Q'(s)-Q'(x)|/|s-x|^(3/2) over x +/- delta x/T(x) is at most epsilon |Q'(x)| sqrt(T(x)/|x|). Given a triangular array chi_n={x_{1,n},...,x_{n,n}}, Cotes numbers lambda_{j,n}, a smooth factor V that decays near the endpoints c and d, p>0, and algebraic polynomials P of degree at most n-1, can one establish forward and converse Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund quadrature estimates of the forms sum_j lambda_{j,n} w(x_{j,n})^(-2) V(x_{j,n}) |P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p <= C integral_I |P(x)w(x)|^p V(x) dx and ||P w||_p <= C (sum_j lambda_{j,n} w(x_{j,n})^(-2) |P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p)^(1/p), establish corresponding polynomial density criteria such as endpoint decay of f w/V, and use these tools to prove mean and uniform convergence of Lagrange interpolation and orthogonal expansions, including rates of convergence?

accepted.question_text: Let I=(c,d) with -infinity <= c < 0 < d <= infinity, and let w:I -> (0,infinity) be an admissible exponential weight satisfying the regularity, endpoint-growth, T-function comparability, and local Lipschitz-type conditions in the admissibility definition: Q=log(1/w), Q(0)=0, Q' is nondecreasing, Q tends to infinity at both endpoints, T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x) is one-sided quasi-monotone and bounded below by a constant greater than 1, T(y) is locally comparable to T(y(1 - epsilon_0/T(y))), and Q' satisfies the stated local integral smoothness bound. Let f be a smooth function such that f w decays at specified endpoint rates, and let k be a specified kernel that typically decays near the endpoints. For the scalar integral I[k,f]=integral_I f(t)k(t) dt, and also for the weighted Hilbert-transform case I[k,f](x)=principal value integral_I (f(t)w(t))/(x-t) dt, define product-integration rules from a node array chi_n by I_n^*[k,f](x)=sum_{j=1}^n w_{j,n}(x) f(x_{j,n}), with the weights w_{j,n} chosen so that the rule reproduces every algebraic polynomial of degree at most n-1. What necessary and sufficient conditions on the admissible weight, the kernel, the function class, and the node arrays guarantee mean convergence and pointwise convergence of these product-integration rules to the corresponding integral?
